# Reconciliation core: normative specification
This section specifies a new reconciliation core.
Historical miniblock designs and measurements elsewhere do not establish its implementation, performance or safety.
This section controls the core where historical descriptions conflict.
## §1 ARCHITECTURE
The core is a sans-IO deterministic state machine.
No sockets, threads, wall clock, globals, or hidden randomness.
Time and an RNG seed are passed in; all output is returned as Actions.
The host serializes all calls (single owner); the core never calls host services.
RootFunction is the explicit exception: a pure deterministic calculation supplied by Configuration, with no IO, mutation, hidden randomness or access to peer ground truth.
```cpp
class SnowstormNode
public:
explicit SnowstormNode(Configuration configuration); // maximumAdversaryFraction, epsilon, maximumSetSize, RootFunction, randomSeed
Actions OnTransactionAdmitted(TransactionHandle, Time);
Actions OnTransactionRemoved(ShortID, RemovalReason, Time);
Actions OnTransactionBodyRemoved(ShortID, TransactionHash, RemovalReason, Time);
Actions OnTransactionBodiesResult(PeerID, ShortID, BodyResult, Time);
Actions OnMessage(PeerID, ByteSpan, Time);
Actions OnTimer(Time);
Actions OnPeerConnected(PeerID, PeerCapabilities, Time);
Actions OnPeerDisconnected(PeerID, Time);
Actions OnNewTip(TipParameters, Time);
Actions OnBlockDisconnected(TipParameters, Time);
NodeStatistics GetStatistics() const;
Action alternatives: Send{peer,bytes}, FetchBody{peer,shortID,fetchID}, Frozen{root,transactionIDs}, PeerMisbehaved{peer,reason}, ScheduleTimer{at}.
RemovalReason is expiry, trim, conflict, reorg, batchLoser, variant, replaced or other.
TransactionHandle is an immutable opaque shared handle exposing 32-byte transactionID, 32-byte transactionHash and shortID.
The core computes current shortID from transactionHash and TipParameters; a cached handle shortID is not authoritative after rekey.
TipParameters contains a 32-byte tip context, SipHash k0/k1 and surviving handles.
PeerID is a nonzero host-assigned connection identity never reused within a node lifetime; a reconnect has a fresh PeerID.
PeerCapabilities contains protocolVersion and positive host-measured RTT.
Only version 2 compatible peers enter D and protocol handling; incompatible peers generate no protocol traffic and are not penalized for incompatibility.
Time is signed int64 monotonic microseconds, with 0 <= Time <= INT64_MAX.
Calls must be nondecreasing in Time.
Backwards times and local arithmetic overflow return no Actions, set NodeStatistics.lastAPIError, and leave protocol state unchanged.
Configuration requires finite 0<=maximumAdversaryFraction<1/3, finite 0<epsilon<1, 1<=maximumSetSize<=floor((2^21−256)/8) and a nonempty RootFunction.
Invalid Configuration throws std::invalid_argument before allocating protocol state.
Remote input never throws out of an API call or reaches an assertion.
The host must keep admitted distinct-ID count and total admitted body count each <=maximumSetSize.
An over-capacity admission is an explicit local API error, not a false successful admission.
Other public operations return typed errors rather than wrapping integers or silently changing operands.
Host contract: every FetchBody token receives exactly one result, even after cancel/reset/disconnect (host owns timeouts).
BodyResult contains fetchID, optional expectedTransactionHash, one of admitted, notFound, invalid or localRejected, and binding status matched or unbound.
The host first parses body bytes and verifies their transactionHash maps to the requested short ID with the request's tip key.
Unparseable/wrong-ID bytes are unbound peer-local failures; they cannot justify global invalid-ID rejection.

Only a matching-ID body that fails actual transaction validation is invalid/matched. admitted requires matched binding, the exact32-byte expectedTransactionHash whose current short ID equals the requested ID, and successful actual admission. localRejected requires matched binding and expectedTransactionHash: a valid bound body was not admitted solely because of local policy/resource/temporary-context constraints, and no global invalidity is established.
The host must not map policy refusal to admitted, notFound or invalid.

On a live token, validate the status and binding enum domains before interpreting status-specific fields. notFound ignores binding/hash fields only after both enum values are valid. invalid/matched requires the matched32-byte hash; invalid/unbound ignores any supplied hash and is donor failure. admitted/unbound, localRejected/unbound, missing/wrong-binding required hashes or illegal enum values on a live token are local HostContractError with no state mutation or peer penalty.
Stale/unknown/completed tokens are ignored before interpreting their payload.
The host sends an admitted result before the matching OnTransactionAdmitted; that callback must eventually follow unless a tip transition cancels its generation.
It never admits merely because an ID decoded.
Tokens increase monotonically across tip/connection generations and never reuse; exhaustion is a nonfatal local error.
Existing admitted matching IDs make late failures obsolete, not grounds for removing an admitted body.
The core never inserts transactions into the host.
RootFunction receives all candidate bodies in canonical (transactionID bytes,transactionHash bytes) lexicographic order; the identity of the tip is an explicit additional RootFunction input.
It returns 32 bytes and must be collision-resistant for honest equality inference.
Frozen contains sorted unique transactionIDs represented by those candidate bodies.
Root equality is a peer assertion, not authentication of a Byzantine peer's bodies.
Out of scope: SnapBlock/Stage1.5, conflict resolution/BatchId, stake weighting and consensus changes.
## §2 FIELD GF(2^64)
P(x)=x^64+x^4+x^3+x+1 (reduction constant 0x1B).
Multiply: hardware carry-less multiply (PMULL/PCLMULQDQ) selected by runtime CPU detection using function target attributes; portable fallback using 4-bit windowed tables.
Squaring: byte tables.
Inverse: Itoh–Tsujii.
Batch inverse: Montgomery's trick.
Invert(0) returns a typed ZeroInverse error.
Batch inverse rejects a batch containing zero atomically with the same error; an empty batch succeeds with empty output.
Solve(D) for u^2+u=D returns false iff Tr(D)=1; otherwise use the even-degree method with theta=x^61 (Tr(theta)=1), byte-wise tables, and verify y^2+y==D before returning.
Solve(0) returns true,y=0.
Half-trace is incorrect in even-degree fields and forbidden.
Runtime backend selection and portable/hardware agreement are observable without exposing mutable dispatch state.
## §3 SHORT IDS AND BODIES
shortID is the 64-bit SipHash-2-4(k0,k1,transactionHash) result; zero maps to one.
The transactionHash argument is exactly its canonical 32-byte sequence, not TransactionID||TransactionHash.
Different witness transactionHash values generally have different IDs but can collide.
R is keyed by distinct shortID; each ID owns its admitted body bucket.
A second distinct body under an ID changes its body view and changes the root only if that ID is in W; it does not change the ID sketch or admission sequence.
Duplicate admission of the same transactionHash is a no-op.

OnTransactionBodyRemoved(id,hash) removes precisely that body, updates the body view immediately, changes the root only for a candidate-body change, and removes the ID and its sketch contribution only when its last body leaves.
Unknown body removal is a no-op.
OnTransactionRemoved(id) is the explicit whole-bucket operation; every body under that ID leaves.
Host normal removal callbacks use the body-specific method.
Every RemovalReason has these same core set semantics.
Sketch reconciliation establishes distinct-ID equality in tested trials, not complete collision-body agreement.
A colliding body can be hidden by the ID sketch, and globally rejecting an authenticated invalid matching-ID body can conservatively suppress a valid colliding body for the height.
These are explicit limitations; ordinary host validation and block fallback remain mandatory.
No claim of collision-complete transaction dissemination is made.
## §4 CODING
### §4.1 Cells and decode
Cell={int32 count;u64 s1,s3,s5}, serialized in 28 bytes little-endian. count never wraps and −2^31 is forbidden: exceeding ±(2^31−1) returns local Overflow or remote PeerMisbehaved(countOverflow).
Adding nonzero x with sign sigma in {−1,+1}: count+=sigma;s1^=x;s3^=x^3;s5^=x^5.
A residual is received cell minus requester reference encoding at the same index.
Decode(residual,idx,inReference) returns Zero, One{x,sigma}, Two{x1,sigma1,x2,sigma2}, or Undecodable:
- Zero iff count=0 and all syndromes zero.
- One requires |count|=1,s1!=0,s3=s1^3,s5=s1^5,ScheduleIncludes(s1,idx), and count=+1 iff s1 absent from reference (−1 iff present).
- Two requires count in {−2,0,+2},s1!=0.
D=1 xor s3*s1^−3; Solve(D) succeeds; x1=s1*u;x2=x1 xor s1.
Require distinct nonzero roots, s5=x1^5 xor x2^5 and schedule inclusion for both.
Each sigma is −1 if root in reference, +1 otherwise; require sigma1+sigma2=count.
Return roots in increasing unsigned order.
- Otherwise Undecodable.
Checks do not authenticate a chosen malicious set; finite syndromes are not an injective commitment for arbitrary large sets.
### §4.2 Integer Rateless IBLT schedule
Credit: Yang et al., SIGCOMM2024.
Item x has i0=0.
SplitMix64 state starts x.
Each step adds 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=(z xor(z>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9; z=(z xor(z>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb; output=z xor(z>>31), all operations u64 modulo arithmetic.
Draw u as low32 bits of exactly one output; s=2^32−u.
Given included i, next j is the least integer j>i with `s*(j+1)*(j+2) >= 2^32*(i+1)*(i+2)`.
Compute with u128 integer square root of the quadratic discriminant and exact integer adjustment.
No floating point.
Stop/exhaust if j>maximumSymbolIndex; never wrap.
The corresponding continuous inverse-CDF has survival (i+1)(i+2)/((j+1)(j+2)), hence marginal inclusion2/(j+2). uint32 quantization is the exact implemented law.
T3 retains target1/(1+i/2), million samples and4σ tolerance.
This discrete law explicitly corrects the former inverse-square formula's .6400000001303852 index1 probability, which was inconsistent with2/3.
### §4.3 Sketch
Encode(set,[a,b)) returns cells.
Incremental cache updates every advertised A membership gain/loss at every cached scheduled index.
Use 64-byte-aligned SoA cell storage and precomputed (x,x^3,x^5) per ID.
Body-only bucket changes do not modify sketches.
Range bounds and overflow are checked before mutation.
### §4.4 Peeler
Use a worklist; each pass snapshots its dirty set; changes requeue cells; attempt singletons before pairs, batch-invert s1^3 for pair candidates and recheck staleness before solving.
Run until empty, without an iteration cap.
Each successful item removal changes reference membership and subtracts that item from every stored scheduled residual exactly once.
A Two event is atomic and removes two distinct items.
The node does not subtract them again.
Keep a per-pass claim ledger of item/sign.
A repeated item claim in the same fixed reply/reference pass is inconsistentSymbols and terminates processing of that reply, not an endlessly toggling +x/−x cycle.
At the node boundary this peel-derived failure is discarded without PeerMisbehaved (§6.6), since shared Pending may contain another peer's fabricated ID.
The reference is fixed at reply-processing entry.
Host changes cannot interleave the serialized call.
Fetch/Pending effects are applied after peeling; they do not mutate the input reference or cause a second subtraction.
Each attempt uses an immutable-input invariant residual and a private working copy; retained replies do not keep raw cells.
The harness independently retains the received wire bytes.

Claimed items beyond the validated maximum possible signed difference are a peel-derived inconsistency, discarded without a peer penalty; storage exhaustion is separately ResourceLimit, never an iteration cap.
No hostile input triggers debug assertions.
Recoverably validate hostile inconsistency and capacity before any internal debug invariant assertion.
Each successful decode audit records its entire original source cell, index, both original membership bits and grouped One/Two outputs before any residual update.
Independently rechecking a Two uses that original pair cell, not two fictitious singleton checks.
Peeler append validates the entire input batch before mutation.

A prohibited INT32_MIN count or reconstruction overflow returns Error::overflow; an out-of-range index returns Error::invalidRange; conflicting duplicate indices, within the batch or against stored raw cells, return Error::inconsistentSymbols; insufficient capacity returns Error::capacity.
Each such error leaves all peeler state unchanged.
Identical duplicate raw cells are no-ops.
## §5 SET STORE
R continues to own all host-admitted body buckets and their bounded item lifetimes.
Define advertised raw A={id in admittedIDs whose state is not FINAL-out}.
Encode A in every own POLL/REPLY and setSize=|A|; exclusions are A minus candidate IDs.
FINAL-out IDs occur in neither cells nor exclusions.
The decode reference is Ref=(A union Pending) minus FINAL-out IDs.
Inbound POLLs decode against A alone.
A is a derived membership filter over existing state, with no second body store.
A gain/loss, including a FINAL-out transition, updates caches and retained invariant residuals exactly once by net reference membership.
Message formulas below use advertised A wherever they name sent/peer raw IDs; host admission/removal capacity still counts all R bodies/IDs, including terminal ones.
R is the host-admitted, not-removed body set of this height, keyed by distinct shortID, each with its admission sequence.
Conflicts are not resolved here.
Retain the conservative rejected-ID exception: a host admission under an ID rejected this height returns RejectedId without insertion, even for a valid colliding body.
This is not an exact host-pool mirror and never bypasses normal validation.
Body buckets, duplicate admission, body-specific removal and sequence behavior remain as specified in §3.
The sketch cache encodes current A at [0,cachedSymbolCount), extending on demand up to maximumSymbolsPerReply.
Sparse probe indices use the same §4 schedule/encoding without allocating a dense array through the largest probe index.
No snapshots, pins or change log are retained.

OnNewTip/OnBlockDisconnected recompute IDs from surviving handles and the new key, clear Pending, confidence, W membership and per-height body-outcome marks, cancel old fetch generations and active rounds, preserve compatible connections and monotonic token generators.
All surviving admitted IDs form W and start with preference in, both cumulative success counters zero, evidence S=0 and no FINAL status; no prior Pending or item state is inherited across tip reset.
Sizing history follows the explicitly bounded rollover in §6.3.
Old asynchronous results cannot mutate the new generation.
## §6 POLLS (STATELESS)
### §6.1 Canonical messages and candidate proof
Concrete wire proposal for approval: u8 version=2, u8 kind (0=POLL,1=REPLY_MATCH,2=REPLY,3=REPLY_DIFF), then tipContext[32] on every message.
This new version prevents confusing old session messages with polls.
Integers are u64LE unless stated, lengths canonical CompactSize, no trailing bytes. pollID is nonzero and strictly increases without reuse per node; exhaustion is a local error.
Exclusions are strictly ascending nonzero IDs.
Fully validate lengths, bounds, integer arithmetic and grammar before allocating message-owned collections.
Incompatible versions do not enter protocol handling.
POLL: pollID, nonce[16], root[32], setSize, mode:u8, n,
m:CompactSize, cells[m]
REPLY_MATCH: pollID, proof[16]
REPLY: pollID, rootVote[32], setSize,
exclusionCount:CompactSize, exclusions[exclusionCount],
m:CompactSize, cells[m]
REPLY_DIFF: pollID, rootVote[32], setSize,
exclusionCount:CompactSize, exclusions[exclusionCount],
missingCount:CompactSize, missing[missingCount],
wantedCount:CompactSize, wanted[wantedCount]
POLL mode=0 requests prefix [0,n); mode=1 requests probe {0} union {2^k−1 <= setSize}, k>=1, sorted/deduplicated and clipped to the shared cell cap by retaining the lowest requested indices.
POLL’s basis is its send-time setSize, not a separate wire field.
Prefix n>=1; probe n=0.
REPLY is always a dense prefix [0,m), including after a probe, and carries neither mode nor basisSize.
There is no redundant REPLY correlation metadata; peer, pollID and tip context correlate it with the current slot.
setSize is own distinct advertised |A| at send/reply time, not |R union Pending|.
POLL carries the poller's own A encoding at exactly the requested indices: prefix[0,n) or the clipped probe set.
Its cells,root and setSize are computed from the same state.
For prefix POLL m=n; for probe m is exactly the prescribed clipped index count.
The receiver validates those identities and cell structure before any Ref-dependent decode.
For fallback prefix REPLY, m=min(maximumSymbolsPerReply,max(2*n,RequiredSymbols(abs(setSizeR−setSizeQ)))).
No successful-decode RequiredSymbols(Delta) reply-cell floor remains: success sends plain IDs instead.

For a probe, compute a transient difference estimate estimatedProbeDifference from its pre-peel residual against responder A using the existing approximate estimator and boundary/censor rules in §6.3; fallback REPLY is prefix[0,m),m=min(maximumSymbolsPerReply,RequiredSymbols(estimatedProbeDifference)).
A censored estimate supplies its lower bound.
This estimate sizes this response only: no inbound sizing-bank sample or retained poll state is created.
There is no largest-probe-index doubling operand.
Discarded contradictory claims are not counted in the estimator lower bound.
Use checked/saturating arithmetic before allocation.
No partial ID lists,leftover residuals or bitmaps are sent in fallback replies.
At the cap the prefix cannot grow further;no unconditional growth beyond the cap is claimed.
Cells, rootVote, setSize and full exclusions=A minus candidate IDs are all computed from one current responder state during the serialized call.
The responder keeps no poll bookkeeping and answers every well-formed POLL; generic rate limiting belongs to the host.
If responder’s candidate root equals the POLL root, send REPLY_MATCH without decoding POLL cells; structural validation still applies.
Otherwise peel the POLL once against responder raw A, not Pending, captured at call entry.
Do not retain or rescue inbound POLL cells.

On success, if the complete DIFF fits the message limit, send missing=negative decoded IDs (responder-only) and wanted=positive decoded IDs (poller-only), each strictly ascending, nonzero and disjoint.

The responder fetches its eligible positive items from the poller through ordinary FetchBody with the existing Pending reservation, binding and alternate-donor lifecycle. wanted describes absence for item votes; it is not a body request and triggers no body-send host action.
Ordinary incomplete inbound positives use that same bounded fetch path.
An explicit contradiction discards all effects of the inbound attempt before fallback.
A decode never inserts R.
Response cells, rootVote, setSize and exclusions refer to one coherent responder state.
On ordinary incomplete decode or explicit peel contradiction, fall back to REPLY with cells using the existing sizing rule; no REPLY_DIFF is emitted.
Peel-derived faults are silent; structural cell faults remain reportable.
Partial positives from an ordinary incomplete inbound attempt follow normal fetch rules.
An explicit contradiction discards ALL effects of that attempt before building fallback REPLY.
If successful decoding produces a complete REPLY_DIFF exceeding the message limit, send fallback REPLY cells instead; never truncate or fragment the ID lists.
Inbound decoding uses raw A so normal Pending assumptions from other peers cannot be used as its reference.
For candidate IDs x, proof is LE64(XOR SipHash-2-4(nonce,0x00||LE64(x))) followed by LE64(XOR SipHash-2-4(nonce,0x01||LE64(x))).
Decode nonce's first/second eight bytes as little-endian k0/k1.
Hash each distinct candidate ID once, regardless of body bucket size; empty XOR=0.
Nonces come from the core's seeded RNG (proposed two consecutive u64 draws serialized LE).
All polls of a round are sent at round start from one state.
Keep ONE round capture: advertised admitted IDs with admission incarnation and candidate bit, plus Pending IDs live at round start with their live item-lifetime identity, at most M+P records total.
No body handles or per-slot copies are retained.
Each slot stores its 16-byte expected proof over captured W and points at that capture.

Only captured item lifetimes still live at scoring time receive this round’s observations; matching Pending admission preserves its lifetime and eligibility, while loss of support or removal/readmission does not.
Items first appearing after capture get no votes this round.
Release the capture at round end or tip reset.
A delayed poll shares the capture only if the captured admitted/candidate/Pending state remains unchanged; otherwise defer it to the next round.
Never create a second capture.
Verify REPLY_MATCH against the stored proof even if current own root has changed.
Mismatch still causes inconsistentReply and abstention; do not discard a valid old-root MATCH merely because a body was admitted meanwhile.
Candidate proof is algebraic set evidence, not authentication of bodies or identities.
The poller keeps fixed current-round slots (peer,pollID,nonce,n,mode,send-time |A|,sent root,sent time,expected proof[16],shared round-capture reference,answer status).
Correlated duplicates cannot contribute twice.
Stale/unknown context or connection generations cannot mutate current evidence.
Discard late replies entirely: no decoding, fetching, sizing, evidence or votes.
No past-round slots are retained.

REPLY_DIFF is a complete reconstruction with no cell peeling or retention; its lists remain unauthenticated peer assertions. peerCandidates=((round capture raw A minus wanted) union missing) minus peer exclusions.
Start from captured raw A, including locally excluded IDs.
For a captured Pending ID absent from captured raw A, the peer holds it exactly when it occurs in missing; use this reconstruction for all eligible captured lifetimes.
Post-capture items receive no observation.
Removal/readmission invalidates old-incarnation observations; matching live Pending admission preserves its state and eligibility.

The poller starts ordinary FetchBody for eligible missing items, deduplicating concurrent in-flight/awaiting operations and preserving alternate-donor retry. wanted triggers no fetch or body-send action at the poller.
Admission remains host-authoritative.
Record estimatedRoundStartDifference=|missing|+|wanted| and estimatedCurrentDifference=|missing minus current Ref|+|wanted intersect current A| at reply-processing entry, before Pending effects.
These are exact counts of the specified lists, not authenticated holdings.
DIFF supplies the normal exact sizing sample and complete per-item observations.

Validate list lengths, strictly ascending nonzero IDs, disjoint missing/wanted, wanted membership in captured raw A and missing absence from captured raw A, and setSize=sentSetSize+missingCount−wantedCount with checked arithmetic.
The asserted peer raw set is (captured raw A minus wanted) union missing; its cardinality must equal setSize and its exclusions must be a subset.
Exclusion and complete-message bounds apply.
Reject an internally inconsistent DIFF before any fetch or observation effect, using captured raw A rather than current R or Pending.
This checks the assertion’s internal consistency and does not authenticate the peer’s holdings.
wanted only describes peer absence for voting.

Body transfers in both directions use ordinary FetchBody from the node that decoded a positive item: the responder fetches positives from the POLL, and the poller fetches missing from DIFF or fallback decoding.
No body-send action or new receive-token protocol exists.
Duplicate/stale replies cannot duplicate operations.
Fallback decoding causes no automatic back-propagation; a node discovers items through its own polls and existing fetch path.
### §6.2 One-call decoding
Capture Ref=(own A union Pending) minus FINAL-out IDs at reply-processing entry and keep it fixed as input for the entire call.
Decode received cells minus Ref's encoding at their indices; every later rescue attempt similarly captures the current Ref at its start.
The peeler's private working reference changes as it peels, not the captured Ref.
Success means all residuals zero.
Decoded items are algebraically consistent, never authenticated holdings.
FetchBody and host validation remain the only authority for admission.
After the arrival peel completes, eligible decoded positive items may start bounded fetches and thereby enter Pending.
No prefix continuation occurs. peerCandidates=((Ref union decodedPositive) minus decodedNegative) minus peerExclusions describes a complete reconstruction only when no residual remains.
Record this round’s item observations from the arrival outcome under §8, before later rescue attempts can discover more items.
An item preference or counter alone never cancels a fetch or creates an epoch rejection mark.
Partial positives still use the normal fetch path.
Successful arrival replies release cell workspace after discovery/observations; ordinary incomplete replies retain indices, exclusions and ONE invariant residual array for dissemination/rescue.
Core retains no second raw-cell array.
Raw cells can be reconstructed as residual+Encode(current Ref); the harness separately owns wire bytes.
Nothing is retained across round end or tip cancellation.
Explicit contradictions discard the reply under the existing nonpunitive policy.
For each retained reply, invariant residual=raw cells−Encode(current Ref) at its indices.
A Ref membership gain/loss applies exactly one signed contribution at the item's scheduled indices in every retained reply.
Update only net Ref membership: Pending-to-A or A-to-Pending transitions preserving membership have no delta.
Admissions, removals, Pending changes, fetch failures and probation use this same rule.
A decoded item never inserts R and never directly changes the invariant buffer; only the Ref change it actually causes does so.
Each peel attempt copies the invariant residual into ONE transient working buffer of at most maximumSymbolsPerReply cells, peels that copy, then discards it.
Charge the buffer within decode workspace.
Never retain private peel subtractions as invariant residuals.
Capture Ref at attempt start for peerCandidates and audit; after peel, apply eligible fetch/Pending effects.
Partial positives follow the same live-fetch rules; they do not authenticate bodies.
Maintain a dirty set ordered by poll order.
A Ref change marks retained replies with touched scheduled indices.
Repeatedly attempt the smallest dirty reply until none is dirty.
A successful rescue reconstructs the peer raw/candidate view against that attempt’s Ref, discovers donors and fetches eligible items, then releases cell workspace.
Rescue contributes no new item observations that round: neither decoded later items nor newly inferred shared items replace arrival abstention.
This includes dirty-set attempts caused within the same API call after the first arrival peel.
Already eligible arrival observations remain governed by their captured lifetime and the existing validity/discard rules.
Ordinary failure leaves the reply retained and clean; contradictions follow §6.6.
Cascading Ref additions can dirty earlier replies; choose the smallest dirty poll order next.
Arrival observations use the existing bounded round-evidence records keyed to captured item lifetimes and selected peers.
Record at most one outcome per selected peer/item; later rescue does not update it.
Ordinary lifetime/validity filters still apply at scoring.
No per-reply cell-index evidence buffer or extra evidence-only peel is retained or run.
Capture/evidence storage is released at round end or tip reset and actual capacities remain charged under §6.5.
No work cap and no proportionality claim.
A retained reply is re-peeled only after a Ref change touches its indices.
Within the cascade of one call, Ref gains at most P new Pending entries and an ID cannot re-enter Pending in that call.
Assert attempts per call<=retained-reply bound*(1+Ref changes in the call), conservatively using K as the reply bound, without terminating at a runtime cap.
Record residual-update touches separately from actual re-peel steps/attempts and rescued replies.
No dirty reply remains when the call finishes.
Admission and root changes do not abandon the round.
Keep eligible item evidence and update retained residuals for net Ref changes, including admission/removal.
There is no separate root-confidence state or root-change scoring veto.
Tip/generation reset still cancels the round.
Rescues use current Ref for dissemination; item observation eligibility and values come from the arrival outcome and the corresponding captured lifetime.

Sizing estimatedCurrentDifference and estimatedRoundStartDifference are captured only at first processing, using its pre-peel bitmap and original attempt's lower bound; later attempts create no new samples and never rewrite earlier ones.
The first peel counts as one attempt.
A residual-delta audit record is per (Ref item,retained reply) pair, not per touched cell.

Full-observation tests record the complete cascade in observation-owned growable storage (§10); audit allocation failure is a test failure, not a protocol ResourceLimit or an atomic-reservation requirement.
Do not reserve a worst-case audit envelope.
Protocol reservations and the attempt/no-dirty assertions remain mandatory.
Inbound POLLs disseminate items only; their reference is own A, distinct from the (A union Pending) minus FINAL-out reference used when decoding received REPLY cells.

They supply no batch vote, no per-transaction vote and no estimatedCurrentDifference/estimatedRoundStartDifference sizing sample: the responder did not select who polls it, and adversaries can poll at will.

Use the existing transient working buffer for one attempt, charge its inbound per-attempt signed-claim bound2*M within the existing per-call claim accounting and observation attempt counters, then release all POLL-cell workspace.
Inbound-triggered fetches use the existing P union reservation.
No inbound poll slot is retained.
Pending additions from an inbound POLL are ordinary Ref changes: update retained outbound residuals and run normal dirty-order rescue.
These rescues disseminate items but do not create or upgrade this round’s item observations.
Inbound polls themselves never gain evidence eligibility or sizing samples.
### §6.3 Adaptive sizing and frozen RequiredSymbols(d)
A timely REPLY_DIFF supplies uncensored start and now samples defined in §6.1.
A fallback REPLY means either inbound decode did not succeed or a complete DIFF exceeded the message limit; apply the existing approximate estimator and growth rule to its cells.
Every timely processed REPLY with cells records which residual cells are zero BEFORE peeling.
Exclude index0 from the likelihood because p0=1; a zero symbol0 is used in the explicit zero-estimate branch below.
For i>=1 use inclusionProbability=2/(i+2) and the model P(empty at i)=(1−inclusionProbability)^Delta.
This is an independence approximation: schedule cells are correlated and mixed-sign cancellation is treated as negligible.
Call the result the approximate maximum-likelihood estimate, not an exact MLE.

## §9 SIMULATOR AND EVALUATION
Rationale: Snowstorm is push-pull gossip.
A random-subset POLL carries the poller's cells, letting the responder discover missing items immediately.
If decoded, the responder returns the signed difference as plain IDs in REPLY_DIFF; otherwise it returns cells in fallback REPLY.
In a successfully decoded nonmatching exchange, cells move into the POLL rather than being added to a cell-bearing reply; fallback exchanges can carry cells in both directions.
One exchange therefore disseminates in both directions rather than requiring a later reverse poll.
Under uniform regular connectivity each node sends K polls and receives about K polls per round in expectation, so polling itself is push-pull.

The intended latency benefit is saving the wait for a reverse poll, described as half a round; actual timing and decode success are measured, not guaranteed. [Karp, Schindelhauer, Shenker and Vöcking, Randomized Rumor Spreading, FOCS2000](https://archive.cone.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/pubs/rumor.pdf) motivates combining directions, not a complete Snowstorm protocol proof.
